claim: Radiotherapy resistance in nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) is a major cause of recurrence and metastasis.
source: Radiotherapy resistance in nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) is a major cause of recurrence and metastasis.
evidence: This is a general statement in the abstract that is supported by established scientific knowledge about NPC treatment outcomes.

claim: The glmBoost+NaiveBayes model was selected to construct the NPC-RSS based on 18 key genes.
source: By evaluating 113 machine learning algorithm combinations, the glmBoost+NaiveBayes model was selected to construct the NPC-RSS based on 18 key genes, which demonstrated good predictive performance in both public and in-house datasets.
evidence: The manuscript describes the methodology and results of model selection based on evaluation of multiple algorithm combinations.

claim: NPC-RSS demonstrated good predictive performance in both public and in-house datasets.
source: By evaluating 113 machine learning algorithm combinations, the glmBoost+NaiveBayes model was selected to construct the NPC-RSS based on 18 key genes, which demonstrated good predictive performance in both public and in-house datasets.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental validation on multiple datasets as described in the manuscript.

claim: NPC-RSS is closely associated with immune features, including chemokine factors and their receptor families and the major histocompatibility complex (MHC).
source: The study found that NPC-RSS is closely associated with immune features, including chemokine factors and their receptor families and the major histocompatibility complex (MHC).
evidence: This finding is based on analysis of immune-related features in the study.

claim: NPC-RSS influences key signaling pathways such as Wnt/β-catenin, JAK-STAT, NF-κB, and T cell receptors.
source: Gene functional analysis revealed that NPC-RSS influences key signaling pathways such as Wnt/β-catenin, JAK-STAT, NF-κB, and T cell receptors.
evidence: This is based on gene functional analysis performed in the study.

claim: SMARCA2 and CD9 gene expression is consistent with NPC-RSS in cell line validation.
source: Cell line validation confirmed that SMARCA2 and CD9 gene expression is consistent with NPC-RSS.
evidence: This is supported by experimental validation using cell lines.

claim: The radiotherapy-sensitive group exhibited richer immune infiltration and activation states.
source: Single-cell analysis revealed that the radiotherapy-sensitive group exhibited richer immune infiltration and activation states.
evidence: This finding is based on single-cell analysis performed in the study.

claim: About 70% of new nasopharyngeal cancer cases occur in Eastern and Southeastern Asia.
source: About 70% of new nasopharyngeal cancer cases occur in Eastern and Southeastern Asia, while the rest are mainly in South-Central Asia, North Africa, and East Africa (Chen et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Chen et al., 2019.

claim: A total of 133,354 new cases of nasopharyngeal cancer were reported, accounting for only 0.7% of all new cancer cases.
source: According to the most recent global cancer statistics, a total of 133,354 new cases of nasopharyngeal cancer were reported, accounting for only 0.7% of all new cancer cases that year (Sung et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Sung et al., 2021.

claim: Hyperfractionated intensity-modulated radiotherapy increases the 3-year overall survival rate in NPC patients from 55.0% to 74.6% compared to conventional fractionated intensity-modulated radiotherapy.
source: With the continuous advancement of radiotherapy technology, recent studies have shown that hyperfractionated intensity-modulated radiotherapy increases the 3-year overall survival rate in these patients from 55.0% to 74.6% compared to conventional fractionated intensity-modulated radiotherapy (You et al., 2023).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to You et al., 2023.

claim: Approximately 20–30% of NPC patients experience locoregional recurrence of the tumor due to radiation resistance.
source: However, approximately 20–30% of patients experience locoregional recurrence of the tumor due to radiation resistance (Lee et al., 2015; Ma and Chan, 2005; Agulnik and Epstein, 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Lee et al., 2015; Ma and Chan, 2005; Agulnik and Epstein, 2008.

claim: Radiotherapy resistance is the main reason for treatment failure in nasopharyngeal cancer patients.
source: Studies have shown that radiotherapy resistance is the main reason for treatment failure in nasopharyngeal cancer patients (Linkous and Yazlovitskaya, 2012; Ribassin-Majed et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Linkous and Yazlovitskaya, 2012; Ribassin-Majed et al., 2017.

claim: 48 models were successfully constructed from 113 machine learning algorithm combinations.
source: As shown in Figure 1, 48 models were successfully constructed, and the area under the curve (AUC) of each model was calculated in both the training and validation sets.
evidence: This is based on the computational analysis described and shown in Figure 1.

claim: The best model combination was found to be glmBoost + NaiveBayes after sample weighting.
source: The best model combination was found to be glmBoost + NaiveBayes after sample weighting: the glmBoost algorithm was used to screen out the most valuable gene features, and then the NaiveBayes algorithm was employed to identify the most reliable model (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is based on the evaluation of model performance as shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The model identified 18 genes as candidate genes for subsequent studies.
source: The model identified 18 genes, which were used as candidate genes for subsequent studies.
evidence: This is a direct result of the model construction process.

claim: The top 5 genes characterized in the NPC-RSS, in order of their contribution to radiotherapy sensitivity and weighting coefficients, are SMARCA2, DMC1, CD9, PSG4, and KNG1.
source: The top 5 genes characterized in the NPC-RSS, in order of their contribution to radiotherapy sensitivity and weighting coefficients, are SMARCA2, DMC1, CD9, PSG4, and KNG1.
evidence: This is based on the analysis of gene contributions in the model.

claim: The genes with absolute values of weight coefficients greater than 10 were SMARCA2, DMC1, KNG1, NTRK3, CLDN1, and CDK5RAP3.
source: The genes with absolute values of weight coefficients greater than 10 were SMARCA2, DMC1, KNG1, NTRK3, CLDN1, and CDK5RAP3 (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is based on the weight coefficients shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The prediction model demonstrated an AUC of 0.996 for the training set.
source: The prediction model constructed using these 18 genes demonstrated good diagnostic efficacy, with an area under the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve (AUC) of 0.996 for the training set.
evidence: This is based on ROC curve analysis of the training set.

claim: The GSE32389 dataset yielded an AUC of 0.823 as an external validation set.
source: The GSE32389 dataset was employed as an external validation set, yielding an AUC of 0.823, which demonstrated the model's robustness.
evidence: This is based on validation using an independent dataset.

claim: The overall sample-weighted AUC for the combined training and validation sets was 0.932.
source: The overall sample-weighted AUC for the combined training and validation sets was 0.932 (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is based on combined analysis shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Differential expression analysis resulted in 2932 differentially expressed genes (DEGs).
source: The genes used to construct the model were derived from our center's NPC transcriptome expression data and underwent differential expression analysis, resulting in 2932 differentially expressed genes (DEGs; Figure 2D).
evidence: This is based on differential expression analysis shown in Figure 2D.

claim: SMARCA2 and CD9 were significantly highly expressed in the sensitive group (p<0.001, t-test).
source: The analysis results showed that SMARCA2 and CD9, among the key genes of NPC-RSS, were significantly highly expressed in the sensitive group (p<0.001, t-test), which was consistent with the expression trend of the key genes in the previously constructed NPC-RSS (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is based on statistical analysis of gene expression in cell lines as shown in Figure 2F.

claim: The sensitivity scores of the sensitive group were significantly higher than those of the resistant group in CNE2 cell lines.
source: The results showed that the sensitivity scores of the sensitive group were significantly higher than those of the resistant group, further confirming the reliability of NPC-RSS (Figure 2I).
evidence: This is based on NPC-RSS scoring of cell line samples as shown in Figure 2I.

claim: The radiosensitive group exhibited a significant elevation in the levels of T follicular helper cells, regulatory T cells (Tregs), and activated NK cells compared to the radioresistant group.
source: The results demonstrated a significant elevation in the levels of T follicular helper cells, regulatory T cells (Tregs), and activated NK cells in the samples from the radiosensitive group compared to those from the radioresistant group (Figure 3A), suggesting that the radiosensitive group exhibited a more immunologically active infiltration profile.
evidence: This is based on immune cell infiltration analysis shown in Figure 3A.

claim: SMARCA2 was significantly positively correlated with resting CD4 + memory T cells.
source: We found that several key genes were highly correlated with immune cells: SMARCA2 was significantly positively correlated with resting CD4 + memory T cells
evidence: This is based on correlation analysis between genes and immune cells.

claim: DMC1 was significantly positively correlated with resting NK cells.
source: DMC1 was significantly positively correlated with resting NK cells
evidence: This is based on correlation analysis between genes and immune cells.

claim: CD9 was significantly positively correlated with resting CD4 + memory T cells.
source: CD9 was significantly positively correlated with resting CD4 + memory T cells
evidence: This is based on correlation analysis between genes and immune cells.

claim: KNG1 was significantly negatively correlated with M1 macrophages, γδ T cells, monocytes, eosinophils, neutrophils, and other immune cell types.
source: KNG1 was significantly negatively correlated with M1 macrophages, γδ T cells, monocytes, eosinophils, neutrophils, and other immune cell types (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is based on correlation analysis shown in Figure 3B.

claim: A total of 28,957 cells were acquired from single-cell transcriptome data, with 22,796 cells from the radiotherapy-sensitive group and 6161 cells from the radiotherapy-resistant group.
source: Following single-cell suspension preparation, library construction, sequencing analysis, and quality control of the obtained data, we acquired transcriptome data for a total of 28,957 cells. Among these, 22,796 cells were derived from the radiotherapy-sensitive group, and 6161 cells were from the radiotherapy-resistant group.
evidence: This is based on single-cell sequencing data processing and quality control.

claim: 17 cell subpopulations were identified through clustering, belonging to seven distinct cell types: T cells, myeloid cells, B cells, epithelial cells, neutrophils, fibroblasts, and mast cells.
source: As illustrated in Figure 4, 17 cell subpopulations were identified through clustering. By examining the expression profiles of cell-type-specific marker genes, we determined that these 17 cell subpopulations belonged to seven distinct cell types: T cells, myeloid cells, B cells, epithelial cells, neutrophils, fibroblasts, and mast cells (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is based on single-cell clustering analysis shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Myeloid cells, epithelial cells, fibroblasts, and mast cells were significantly more abundant in samples from the radiotherapy-sensitive group compared to the radiotherapy-resistant group.
source: Myeloid cells, epithelial cells, fibroblasts, and mast cells were significantly more abundant in samples from the radiotherapy-sensitive group compared to the radiotherapy-resistant group.
evidence: This is based on single-cell analysis comparing cell type abundances between groups.

claim: The predicted scores of cells in the sensitive group were significantly higher than those in the resistant group, especially in epithelial cells, myeloid cells, fibroblasts, and mast cells.
source: We used NPC-RSS to calculate the radiotherapy sensitivity scores of each cell. The predicted scores of cells in the sensitive group were significantly higher than those in the resistant group, especially in epithelial cells, myeloid cells, fibroblasts, and mast cells (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is based on NPC-RSS scoring at the single-cell level shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The radiotherapy-sensitive group showed significant dominance in terms of immune cells, whereas the radiotherapy-resistant group was mainly composed of malignant epithelial and stromal cells.
source: Interestingly, the radiotherapy-sensitive group showed significant dominance in terms of immune cells, whereas the radiotherapy-resistant group was mainly composed of malignant epithelial and stromal cells (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is based on cell type composition analysis shown in Figure 4E.

claim: High expression of SMARCA2 enriched signaling pathways such as WNT_BETA_CATENIN_SIGNALING, PI3K_AKT_MTOR_SIGNALING, TGF_BETA_SIGNALING, and NOTCH_SIGNALING.
source: GSVA results demonstrated that high expression of SMARCA2 enriched signaling pathways such as WNT_BETA_CATENIN_SIGNALING, PI3K_AKT_MTOR_SIGNALING, TGF_BETA_SIGNALING, and NOTCH_SIGNALING (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is based on GSVA analysis shown in Figure 5A.

claim: High expression of DMC1 enriched INTERFERON_GAMMA_RESPONSE and IL2_STAT5_SIGNALING pathways.
source: Similarly, high expression of DMC1 enriched INTERFERON_GAMMA_RESPONSE and IL2_STAT5_SIGNALING pathways (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is based on GSVA analysis shown in Figure 5B.

claim: SMARCA2 was enriched in pathways such as the JAK-STAT signaling pathway, NF-kappa B signaling pathway, and T cell receptor signaling.
source: Moreover, GSEA results showed that SMARCA2 was enriched in pathways such as the JAK-STAT signaling pathway, NF-kappa B signaling pathway, and T cell receptor signaling (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is based on GSEA analysis shown in Figure 5C.

claim: DMC1 was enriched in pathways such as cell adhesion molecules, Hedgehog signaling pathway, and phosphatidylinositol signaling system.
source: DMC1 was enriched in pathways such as cell adhesion molecules, Hedgehog signaling pathway, and phosphatidylinositol signaling system (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is based on GSEA analysis shown in Figure 5D.

claim: The expression of SMARCA2 was positively correlated with high expression levels of TP53, EGFR, BRCA2, and ATM.
source: Spearman correlation analysis indicated that the expression of SMARCA2 was positively correlated with high expression levels of TP53, EGFR, BRCA2, and ATM.
evidence: This is based on Spearman correlation analysis of gene expression.

claim: DMC1 expression was positively correlated with high expression levels of BRCA1, APTX, ATM, and CCR6.
source: Similarly, DMC1 expression was positively correlated with high expression levels of BRCA1, APTX, ATM, and CCR6
evidence: This is based on Spearman correlation analysis of gene expression.

claim: CD9 expression was positively correlated with high expression levels of EGFR, TP53, ERBB2, and RAD51.
source: while CD9 expression was positively correlated with high expression levels of EGFR, TP53, ERBB2, and RAD51.
evidence: This is based on Spearman correlation analysis of gene expression.

claim: The expression of KNG1 was correlated with high expression levels of HULC and significantly negatively correlated with high expression levels of BADA.
source: The expression of KNG1 was correlated with high expression levels of HULC and significantly negatively correlated with high expression levels of BADA (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is based on correlation analysis shown in Figure 5E.

claim: SMARCA2 plays a crucial role in various cellular processes, including cytokine response, DNA repair, regulation of cell proliferation, lineage specification and development, and cell adhesion.
source: The protein encoded by the SMARCA2 gene plays a crucial role in various cellular processes, including cytokine response, DNA repair, regulation of cell proliferation, lineage specification and development, and cell adhesion (Helming et al., 2014; Wang et al., 2014; Zhu et al., 2015; Tian et al., 2013; Dykhuizen et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claim: SMARCA2 depletion can increase the sensitivity to radiotherapy in non-small cell lung cancer.
source: Previous studies have shown that SMARCA2 has a significant effect on the responsiveness to radiotherapy in non-small cell lung cancer, and its depletion can increase the sensitivity to radiotherapy, suggesting that SMARCA2 may be a potential therapeutic target for sensitization to radiotherapy (Zernickel et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Zernickel et al., 2019.

claim: DMC1 is a key factor in homologous recombination involved in the repair process of DNA double-strand breaks.
source: DMC1, a key factor in homologous recombination, is involved in the repair process of DNA double-strand breaks (Dunne et al., 2003; Zhang et al., 2017; Xie et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Dunne et al., 2003; Zhang et al., 2017; Xie et al., 2019.

claim: CD9 is believed to play a role in various stages of cancer development.
source: CD9 is believed to play a role in various stages of cancer development (Murayama et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Murayama et al., 2015.

claim: All human PSGs initiate TGF-β1.
source: It has been shown that all human PSGs initiate TGF-β1. In vivo, PSGs may increase the availability of active TGF-β1 in both soluble and matrix-bound forms of this potential cytokine (Warren et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Warren et al., 2018.

claim: TGF-β1 levels accurately predict radiosensitization in elderly patients with unresectable NSCLC undergoing 3D-CRT.
source: Furthermore, TGF-β1 levels accurately predict radiosensitization in elderly patients with unresectable NSCLC undergoing 3D-CRT (Fu et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Fu et al., 2014.

claim: Proteins related to the Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathway (DKK-3, β-catenin, and c-MYC) are involved in the development of NPC.
source: Previous studies have demonstrated that proteins related to the Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathway (DKK-3, β-catenin, and c-MYC) are involved in the development of NPC, and that knockdown of FOXO3a promotes radioresistance in NPC through the Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathway (Pang et al., 2019; Luo et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Pang et al., 2019; Luo et al., 2019.

claim: Knockdown of FOXO3a promotes radioresistance in NPC through the Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathway.
source: Previous studies have demonstrated that proteins related to the Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathway (DKK-3, β-catenin, and c-MYC) are involved in the development of NPC, and that knockdown of FOXO3a promotes radioresistance in NPC through the Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathway (Pang et al., 2019; Luo et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Pang et al., 2019; Luo et al., 2019.

claim: SMARCA2 may regulate the radiosensitivity of NPC via the Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathway.
source: Therefore, we hypothesized that SMARCA2 may regulate the radiosensitivity of NPC via the Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathway.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on inference from pathway analysis and previous literature.

claim: Irradiated tumors can act as adjuvants to the immune system, promoting local tumor control and inducing regression of distant tumor deposits through abscopal effects.
source: Indeed, recent preclinical studies have demonstrated that irradiated tumors can act as adjuvants to the immune system, promoting local tumor control and inducing regression of distant tumor deposits through abscopal effects (Ngwa et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Ngwa et al., 2018.

claim: Radiation significantly alters the distribution of tumor antigens, recruits anti-tumor T cells, and induces a distinct inflammatory microenvironment.
source: In addition to potential systemic effects, radiation significantly alters the distribution of tumor antigens, recruits anti-tumor T cells, and induces a distinct inflammatory microenvironment (Demaria et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Demaria et al., 2021.

claim: Tumors with high immune cell infiltration are more sensitive to radiation.
source: Some studies have shown that tumors with high immune cell infiltration are more sensitive to radiation (Grass et al., 2022)
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Grass et al., 2022.

claim: Over one-third of tumor types in the radiotherapy-sensitive group of solid tumors exhibit an enrichment of CD8 + T cells, M1 macrophages, and NK + cells.
source: Studies have demonstrated that over one-third of tumor types in the radiotherapy-sensitive group of solid tumors exhibit an enrichment of CD8 + T cells, M1 macrophages, and NK + cells (Grass et al., 2022).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Grass et al., 2022.

claim: Samples were collected from 34 NPC patients treated at Zhujiang Hospital of Southern Medical University between March 2017 and July 2021.
source: Additionally, we collected samples from 34 NPC patients treated at Zhujiang Hospital of Southern Medical University between March 2017 and July 2021 (in-house cohort).
evidence: This describes the data collection methodology.

claim: Written informed consent was obtained from the NPC patients whose NPC tissues were collected, and the study was approved by the Ethics Committee of Zhujiang Hospital of Southern Medical University.
source: Written informed consent was obtained from the NPC patients whose NPC tissues were collected, and the study was approved by the Ethics Committee of Zhujiang Hospital of Southern Medical University.
evidence: This describes the ethical approval and consent process.

claim: Differential analysis identified 71 DEGs (p<0.05 and |LogFC|>0.585).
source: This analysis identified 71 DEGs (p<0.05 and |LogFC|>0.585, Supplementary file 2; Liu et al., 2015).
evidence: This is based on differential expression analysis with specified statistical criteria.

claim: 113 combinations of machine learning algorithms were integrated for model construction.
source: We combined these algorithms with the others to form 113 combinations of machine learning algorithms.
evidence: This describes the methodology for model construction.

claim: The CNE2 nasopharyngeal carcinoma cell line was cultured in RPMI 1640 medium supplemented with 10% fetal bovine serum and 1% penicillin/streptomycin.
source: The CNE2 nasopharyngeal carcinoma cell line, previously preserved by the Pearl River Hospital Center for Translational Medicine, was cultured in RPMI 1640 medium supplemented with 10% fetal bovine serum and 1% penicillin/streptomycin.
evidence: This describes the cell culture methodology.

claim: Each T25 culture flask was seeded with approximately 2x10^5 cells in the exponential growth phase and sequentially irradiated with increasing doses (2, 4, 6, 8, and 10 Gy) twice, followed by a single 10 Gy dose, for a total of nine irradiations and a cumulative dose of 50 Gy.
source: Each T25 culture flask was seeded with approximately 2x105 cells in the exponential growth phase and sequentially irradiated with increasing doses (2, 4, 6, 8, and 10 Gy) twice, followed by a single 10 Gy dose, for a total of nine irradiations and a cumulative dose of 50 Gy.
evidence: This describes the experimental protocol for creating radiation-resistant cells.

claim: The CIBERSORT algorithm was applied to analyze the expression data of nasopharyngeal cancer patients to infer the relative proportions of 22 immune-infiltrating cells.
source: The CIBERSORT algorithm was applied to analyze the expression data of nasopharyngeal cancer patients to infer the relative proportions of 22 immune-infiltrating cells.
evidence: This describes the methodology for immune infiltration analysis.

claim: After quality control, 28,957 high-quality NPC cells were retained for further analysis.
source: After quality control, 28,957 high-quality NPC cells were retained for further analysis.
evidence: This describes the result of quality control in single-cell analysis.

claim: The NPC-RSS key genes are closely associated with the level of immune cell infiltration and play a crucial role in the immune microenvironment.
source: These analyses suggest that the NPC-RSS key genes are closely associated with the level of immune cell infiltration and play a crucial role in the immune microenvironment.
evidence: This is an inference based on the correlation analyses performed.

claim: The radiosensitive group exhibited a more immunologically active infiltration profile.
source: The results demonstrated a significant elevation in the levels of T follicular helper cells, regulatory T cells (Tregs), and activated NK cells in the samples from the radiosensitive group compared to those from the radioresistant group (Figure 3A), suggesting that the radiosensitive group exhibited a more immunologically active infiltration profile.
evidence: This is an inference based on the immune cell infiltration data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The presence of immune cells might have influenced the tumor's responsiveness to treatment to some extent prior to radiation therapy.
source: This finding suggests that the presence of immune cells might have influenced the tumor's responsiveness to treatment to some extent prior to radiation therapy.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the single-cell analysis results.

claim: Tumors with a predominance of immune cells may be more likely to exhibit a positive response to radiation therapy.
source: Tumors with a predominance of immune cells may be more likely to exhibit a positive response to radiation therapy, either due to the involvement of immune cells in tumor surveillance and clearance or because the responsiveness of tumors to radiation therapy is modulated by immune cells.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the observed patterns.

claim: NPC-RSS key genes may influence radiotherapy sensitivity in NPC patients through pathways such as WNT_BETA_CATENIN_SIGNALING, JAK-STAT signaling, NF-kappa B signaling, and T cell receptor signaling.
source: These findings suggest that NPC-RSS key genes may influence radiotherapy sensitivity in NPC patients through these pathways.
evidence: This is an inference based on pathway enrichment analysis results.

claim: The radiosensitivity estimated by the NPC-RSS may be associated with a distinct tumor immune microenvironment, which could potentially be exploited through a combinatorial immunotherapy approach.
source: These findings suggest that the radiosensitivity estimated by the NPC-RSS may be associated with a distinct tumor immune microenvironment, which could potentially be exploited through a combinatorial immunotherapy approach.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the immune microenvironment analysis.

claim: T cells expressed CD3D, CD8A, and CD4 genes.
source: T cells expressed CD3D, CD8A, and CD4 genes.
evidence: This describes the marker genes used for cell type identification in single-cell analysis.

claim: Myeloid cells expressed C1QB, LYZ, and AIF1 genes.
source: Myeloid cells expressed C1QB, LYZ, and AIF1 genes.
evidence: This describes the marker genes used for cell type identification in single-cell analysis.

claim: B cells expressed MS4A1 and CD79A genes.
source: B cells expressed MS4A1 and CD79A genes.
evidence: This describes the marker genes used for cell type identification in single-cell analysis.

claim: Epithelial cells specifically expressed KRT5 and EPCAM genes.
source: Epithelial cells specifically expressed KRT5 and EPCAM genes.
evidence: This describes the marker genes used for cell type identification in single-cell analysis.

claim: Fibroblasts expressed DCN and COL1A1 genes.
source: Fibroblasts expressed DCN and COL1A1 genes.
evidence: This describes the marker genes used for cell type identification in single-cell analysis.

claim: Mast cells expressed CPA3, TPSAB1, and MS4A2 as marker genes.
source: Mast cells expressed CPA3, TPSAB1, and MS4A2 as marker genes.
evidence: This describes the marker genes used for cell type identification in single-cell analysis.

claim: Most of the 18 genes in the NPC-RSS were related to immune cells.
source: Moreover, most of the 18 genes in the NPC-RSS were related to immune cells (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is based on gene expression patterns shown in Figure 4D.

claim: T cells, myeloid cells, epithelial cells, mast cells, and fibroblasts consisted of multiple cell subpopulations.
source: It is noteworthy that T cells, myeloid cells, epithelial cells, mast cells, and fibroblasts consisted of multiple cell subpopulations (Figure 4F), suggesting that these cell types may be heterogeneous.
evidence: This is based on single-cell analysis shown in Figure 4F, with inference about heterogeneity.

claim: The expression of SMARCA2 and CD9 in CNE2-RS radiation-resistant cells was consistent with the expression trend of the key genes in the previously constructed NPC-RSS.
source: The analysis results showed that SMARCA2 and CD9, among the key genes of NPC-RSS, were significantly highly expressed in the sensitive group (p<0.001, t-test), which was consistent with the expression trend of the key genes in the previously constructed NPC-RSS (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is based on experimental validation in cell lines shown in Figure 2F.

claim: The 18 gene features exhibited significant differential expression between the sensitive and resistant groups.
source: Furthermore, these 18 gene features exhibited significant differential expression between the sensitive and resistant groups (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is based on differential expression analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: NPC-RSS can serve as a predictive tool for radiotherapy sensitivity in NPC.
source: NPC-RSS can serve as a predictive tool for radiotherapy sensitivity in NPC, offering new insights for precise screening of patients who may benefit from radiotherapy.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the overall study findings.
